items.title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada
items.description: Polling suggests most Albertans favour remaining part of the country, although the debate alone has proven divisive.

items.title: Kenya pastor accused of ordering parents to starve their children to death faces verdict
items.description: Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie faces 191 murder charges - all but one of them children.

items.title: Funding shortages force World Food Programme to cut aid to Gaza
items.description: The number of people helped by the UN agency in the Palestinian territory will drop by about a third - from 1.6 million to 1.1 million.

items.title: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
items.description: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.

items.title: Personal attacks fire up debate before Brazil's run-off vote
items.description: The race heats up just days before the run-off between the left-wing incumbent and his right-wing challenger.

items.title: Italian PM Meloni to hold emergency meeting after weekend of violent clashes
items.description: More than 200 people were detained during two days of rioting in the city, Italian media reports.

items.title: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
items.description: Saudi Arabia said it executed two Bangladeshis last week for committing an "indecent act" in a mosque.

items.title: Possible wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane likely to be trees, say researchers
items.description: Researchers travelled to a remote Pacific Island to confirm whether an object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the mystery of the pilot's disappearance.

items.title: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
items.description: The blaze that killed four men and injured dozens of others spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.

items.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff survives shooting attempt in Mumbai
items.description: Videos showed gunmen firing shots at Shroff's car while it was moving slowly past a crowd.

items.title: Bomb threat forces Israel to Austria flight into emergency landing
items.description: The Airbus jet landed safely in Bulgaria and all passengers and crew aboard were unharmed, officials said.

items.title: EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says
items.description: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies says the country has been "bundled together" in measures aimed at curbing cheap imports.

items.title: Musk and Anthropic pledge public share giveaways
items.description: Musk's announcement comes after Anthropic pledged to create a public benefit fund ahead of its blockbuster stock market listing.

items.title: Australian Greens senator denies claims of misconduct towards women
items.description: Jordon Steele-John says the timing of the claims is motivated by "nasty political games" within the Greens.

items.title: Katya Adler: France's government under pressure after weekend of widespread violence
items.description: Political tension grips France after rioting marred protests over the cost of living and struggling public services, Katya Adler writes.

items.title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia
items.description: Two men tell of the work they say they have been doing to support Ukrainian intelligence during the war.

items.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
items.description: BBC News hears from users, dealers, prison and recovery workers as the country battles with a deadly new drug epidemic.

items.title: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
items.description: Satellite images give clues about how Kim spends his holidays - something far out of reach for most North Koreans.

items.title: The uncertain future of Canada's 30 rescued belugas
items.description: An international rescue operation for the last 30 captive whales in Canada made headlines. Then five of them died.

items.title: Inside Chicago's battle against the synthetic drugs flooding the US
items.description: The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from Chicago, where communities are battling a new wave of synthetic drugs.
